claims.text: What the image looks like RV strain, septal flattening, RV/LV ratio >1 → massive / submassive PE
claims.quote: RV strain, septal flattening, RV/LV ratio >1 Massive / submassive PE

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Filling defect in a pulm a. (the PE itself)
claims.quote: Intraluminal filling defect in pulmonary artery (CT-PA) Pulmonary embolism (gold standard)

claims.text: CTA can show PE severity, for ex by the size of the Rt ventricle or reflux into the hepatic veins
claims.quote: It can also give more information about other lung pathology (eg, demonstration of pneumonia rather than PE as a cause of hypoxia or pleuritic chest pain) as well as severity of PE (for example by the size of the right ventricle or the reflux into the hepatic veins).

claims.text: Echo = most commonly used for risk stratification; RV dilate and hypokinesis may suggest the need for more aggressive therapy
claims.quote: Echocardiography may show a clot in the right atrium or ventricle, but echocardiography is most commonly used for risk stratification in acute PE. The presence of right ventricular dilation and hypokinesis may suggest the need for more aggressive therapy.

claims.text: On echo (her chart): RV dilate, septal flattening, McConnell sign (apical sparing) → acute PE w RV strain
claims.quote: RV dilation, septal flattening, McConnell sign (apical sparing) Acute PE with RV strain

claims.text: Eti ↑risk (massive): impaired RV funct causing hypotension: systol BP < 90 mm Hg or a drop of ≥ 40 mm Hg from baseline for 15 minutes
claims.quote: High risk (massive): Impaired right ventricular function causing hypotension, as defined by systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a drop in systolic blood pressure of ≥ 40 mm Hg from baseline for a period of 15 minutes

claims.text: Intermed risk (submassive): impaired RV funct w.o hypotension: RV enlrg and/or hypokinesis on imaging plus ↑biomarkers (eg, troponin, BNP)
claims.quote: Intermediate risk (submassive): Impaired right ventricular function without hypotension. This is evidenced by right ventricular enlargement and/or hypokinesis on imaging (eg, CT angiography, echocardiography) as well as by increases in circulating biomarkers (eg, troponin, brain natriuretic peptide).

claims.text: Mech: a lrg Emb occluding major pulm arteries (or many smaller emboli occluding much of the dist bed) raises RV P, which may lead to acute RV failure, shock or sudden death
claims.quote: When a large embolus acutely occludes major pulmonary arteries or when many smaller emboli combine to occlude a significant proportion of the more distal vessels, RV pressure increases, which may lead to acute RV failure, shock, or sudden death.

claims.text: Sx Massive PE may manifest w hypotension, tachy, light-headedness/presyncope, syncope, or ♡ arrest
claims.quote: Massive pulmonary emboli may manifest with hypotension, tachycardia, light-headedness/presyncope, syncope, or cardiac arrest.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: consider thrombolysis; ICU
Her chart (echo): CTPA; thrombolysis if massive
↑risk/massive PE and certain intermed risk/submassive PE should be considered for thrombolytic therapy or embolectomy
claims.quote: Patients with high risk/massive PE and certain patients with intermediate risk/submassive PE should be considered for thrombolytic therapy or embolectomy.

claims.text: Thrombolysis or embolectomy = indicated for hypotension that does ⍉resolve after fluid resuscitation, and for selected pts w impaired RV funct or escalating O2 requirements
claims.quote: Rapid reduction of clot burden via thrombolytic therapy or embolectomy is indicated for patients with hypotension that does not resolve after fluid resuscitation, and for selected patients with impaired RV function or escalating oxygen requirements.
